title: COVID-19 Mortality and Vaccination Coverage Among Older Adults in Tunisia, 2020–2022: A National Descriptive and Ecological Study
content: Background: Older adults experienced a disproportionate burden of COVID-19 mortality, but national evidence is limited. We described COVID-19 mortality among adults aged ≥65 years (March 2020–December 2022) and vaccination coverage among the campaign-eligible population aged ≥60 years (March 2021–December 2022). Methods: We conducted a retrospective national descriptive and ecological study using mortality surveillance data from the National Observatory of New and Emerging Diseases (ONMNE) and aggregated data from the national COVID-19 vaccination platform (EVAX). We calculated mortality, age-standardized, and proportional mortality rates; vaccination coverage; dropout proportions; and no-show rates. Results: Of 29,306 COVID-19 deaths, 20,467 (69.8%) occurred among adults aged ≥65 years; 8,725 (42.6%) were aged ≥80 years and 11,463 (56.0%) were male. Cumulative mortality was 1,809.9 per 100,000, with the highest period-specific rate during Delta predominance (750.1 per 100,000). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to adults aged ≥75 years, the only band fully covered by both data sources, mortality was 3,306.4 per 100,000. Coverage among adults aged ≥60 years was 95.4% for at least one dose, 88.3% for a complete schedule, and 38.4% for a third dose; cumulative uptake was 215.1 doses per 100. Coverage varied by governorate, and no-show rates increased in 2022. Governorate-level correlations between coverage and mortality were weak and not statistically significant (age-standardized mortality, Spearman ρ = −0.06, p = 0.77; governorate-specific mortality, ρ = −0.28, p = 0.18). Conclusions: Mortality was concentrated among the oldest-old and during Delta predominance. Coverage was high nationally but uneven geographically, and booster uptake and attendance declined. Targeted outreach and equitable access remain priorities.
